Ericsson Cradlepoint · NCOS SDK sample

IFTTT Rule Engine

Build router automations without writing code

The IFTTT Rule Engine puts an if this, then that rule builder on an Ericsson Cradlepoint router. Pick a condition, such as a status value, a time, or a GPS location, pick an action, and save. The router checks the rule every 10 seconds by default and, when it matches, sets config, sends an alert, or logs a message on its own.

Rules, not code

Drop conditions and actions onto a rule card, press Save rule(s), and the router runs it. Each rule is its own appdata entry, so it survives reboots.

Five ways to say if

IF and WHILE check any config or status path. WHILE can also gate on a time window, WHEN fires on a schedule, and WHERE uses the router's GPS.

Three ways to say then

Set config writes a value to a router path, Send alert raises a router alert for Ericsson NetCloud Manager, and Log message writes to the router log.

How it works

  
Everything runs on the router: a web page to build rules, appdata to keep them, and one evaluation loop per rule.

  

    

      
 Build it, save it, and it runs

      
Save rule(s) writes each rule to appdata as ifttt_rule_<id>. Every 5 seconds
        the engine syncs saved rules and starts each enabled one. After a reboot it waits for
        120 seconds of uptime, then starts every enabled rule again. There is no hard limit on rules.

    

    

      
 Polling or callback

      
Polling interval evaluates the rule every 10 seconds by default (seconds, minutes, or hours),
        and checks every second while a sustain timer is running. Callback uses cp.register
        on each condition's path and evaluates only when that value changes. Not every path sends change
        events, so test first.

    

    

      
 Sustain and logic

      
IF is stateless: it matches on every evaluation while it is true. WHILE and WHERE can require the
        condition to hold for a duration or for N consecutive polls, and any false check resets
        the timer. All (AND) needs every condition; Any (OR) needs one.

    

    

      
 Time and place

      
WHEN fires inside a 60-second window after its time: Once, Every (with an optional FOR limit),
        or X Times, and resets each day. WHILE time windows can wrap midnight. WHERE reads
        status/gps/fix on every evaluation and measures the distance to a target in km or mi.

SDK Data settings

    
Nothing is required. The app picks its own web port the first time it runs, and the rules page writes the rule entries for you.

    

      

        
          
SettingRequiredDefaultValuesWhat it does

        
        
          

            ifttt_web_port
            No
            First free port from 8000, then saved
            1024 to 65535
            Web UI port. Set it to pin the port; delete it and restart to pick one automatically again. If the value is invalid or the port stays busy, the app stops and logs why.
          

          

            ifttt_rule_<id>
            No
            None
            Rule JSON
            One entry per saved rule, written by the web dashboard. The app finds rules by scanning appdata for this prefix, and deleting a rule removes only its entry.
          

        
      

    

    
    
      
  • Set ifttt_web_port in Ericsson NetCloud Manager under the device or group's SDK Data, then restart the app.
    • 
      
  • Open the web UI at http://router_ip:<port>. The port is in the app log, for example Web server started on port 8000. It comes up after the 120-second uptime wait.
    • 
      
  • From the LAN, add a zone firewall forward from the Primary LAN Zone to the Router Zone. Through NetCloud Manager, use LAN Manager with HTTP to 127.0.0.1 and the app's port. The page has no login, so keep that access to trusted networks.
    • 
      
  • Needs NCOS 7.25 or later. WHERE conditions need a GPS module with a fix.
    • 
      
  • To move a rule to another router, use Copy rule and add the JSON to that router's appdata or post it to /api/rules.
    •
